prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the best attorney for you depends on the facts of your crash, the severity of injuries, whether liability is disputed, and your personal preferences (trial experience, communication style, fee structure, location). I can help you find the best fit. Below are practical steps, reputable resources, and a short list of well-known Chicago firms to consider.

How to find the best attorney for your car-accident claim
- Prioritize experience with motor-vehicle collisions and trial experience if your case may go to court.
- Look for a track record of verdicts/settlements for similar injuries (whiplash vs. catastrophic injury).
- Check peer-review ratings and client reviews (Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Avvo, Google/Yelp).
- Verify license and disciplinary record through the Illinois Attorney Registration & Disciplinary Commission (ARDC).
- Confirm contingency-fee terms and whether the firm advances litigation costs.
- Meet 2–3 lawyers for free consultations and compare answers to the same questions.

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many go to trial?
- Have you handled cases like mine (similar injuries/circumstances)?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (partner, associate, paralegal)?
- What is your contingency fee and what costs will I be responsible for if we don’t win?
- What is a realistic timeline and likely outcome for my case?
- Can you provide recent client references or settlements/verdicts?

Resources to find and vet attorneys
- Super Lawyers (Illinois personal injury list)
- Best Lawyers (Chicago personal injury listings)
- Martindale-Hubbell peer-review ratings
- Avvo and Google reviews for client feedback
- Illinois ARDC to check license/discipline
- Chicago Bar Association referral service

A few reputable Chicago personal-injury firms (frequently recommended for car-accident work)
- Clifford Law Offices
- Romanucci & Blandin
- Schiller DuCanto & Fleck
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard
- Power Rogers & Smith

(These are examples of established firms known for personal-injury work; you should still vet any lawyer personally.)

Typical fee and what to expect
- Most personal-injury lawyers take cases on contingency (commonly ~33%–40% of recovery plus litigation costs).
- Many offer a free initial consultation and will handle investigations, medical liens, and negotiating with insurers.
- If liability is contested or injuries are severe, cases may take many months or longer; many settle without trial, but trial-capable lawyers can increase leverage.

If you want, tell me:
- Your zip code/neighborhood,
- Brief facts (severity of injuries, who is at fault, police report, uninsured motorist involved?),
and I’ll shortlist 3–5 Chicago attorneys or firms that match your needs and give contact/next-step suggestions.
